paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: sin matters to God, even the kind you didn't mean to do. The LORD says this is for the one who sins "unintentionally" (Leviticus 4:2), and then He goes right down the line: the anointed priest, the whole assembly, a leader, a common person. Nobody gets skipped, and nobody gets to say "I didn't know." Even the highest title in the camp doesn't come with an undo button (Leviticus 4:3, 22).

But look at what comes next, because this is the good part. Every single time the person becomes aware of the sin, there is a way back: the priest makes atonement, and "he will be forgiven" (Leviticus 4:26). The person who realizes it must confess (Leviticus 5:5), and forgiveness is waiting on the other side. He isn't hiding the door, friend, He's pointing at it.

And He made that door wide enough for everybody: if a lamb costs too much, bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and if the birds cost too much, bring fine flour (Leviticus 5:7, 11). The priest makes atonement, and "he will be forgiven" (Leviticus 5:10, 13). SAME forgiveness, SMALLER wallet! So when you realize you've missed it, don't hide in the back of a junk drawer like I did, baker, but come to the LORD, confess, and know that He has made a way for you to be forgiven.
